I couldn't find how to declare a list of items inside a request body in these FastAPI doc excerpts. They cover single models and multiple separate body parameters, but not list or nested fields.

Here's what they do cover:

- **Bodies are declared with Pydantic models:** To declare a **request** body, you use Pydantic models with all their power and benefits.[1]

  ```python
  from fastapi import FastAPI
  from pydantic import BaseModel


  class Item(BaseModel):
      name: str
      description: str | None = None
      price: float
      tax: float | None = None


  app = FastAPI()


  @app.post("/items/")
  async def create_item(item: Item):
      return item
  ```

- **Multiple models in one body:** if you declare more than one model parameter, it will then use the parameter names as keys (field names) in the body[5]. This gives you something like `{"item": {...}, "user": {...}}`, but not a list.

For an order containing a list of items, see the **"Body - Nested Models"** page of the FastAPI tutorial (https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/body-nested-models/). It covers list fields and models nested inside other models.
